record.title: Permanent Haunting-write failures retain expanding observation histories
record.description: A plugin Credential holder can send small valid detection Events with unique 180-character IDs. The public DTO and Event schema accept those IDs, but createObservations appends :detected:<rule> and sends that longer value to an internal DTO capped at 180 characters. Each write is therefore permanently refused after the accepted WatcherOutcome has entered the daemon's pending map. The consumer's five-delivery limit eventually stops retrying the broker record without notifying or evicting the cached outcome. With timestamps spaced by the watcher dedupe interval, later failed Events for the same bound service retain successive cloned histories containing one, two, three and more detections. This yields source-visible quadratic retained history across a linear number of small Events in the daemon shared by other granted Projects. No heap measurement, crash or service outage has been observed.
record.claimed_root_cause: The in-memory pending outcome cache has success-only cleanup and no terminal-failure, size or expiry policy. Public Event-ID validation is incompatible with derived internal idempotency-key limits, supplying a deterministic permanent-error trigger. createGrouper returns a deep clone of each cumulative group, so each abandoned pending outcome retains its own history rather than only one bounded reference.

trace.description: A Credential holder can choose a nonempty 180-character low-entropy alphabetic ID. The small envelope fits the API size limit and can use its bound service.
Preparation and publication retain the caller's ID after Project/service authorization. An unassigned Event audit key with this ID still fits the core 200-character audit-key contract.
The watcher is mutated and its accepted outcomes are saved in pending before any durable Haunting write completes.
Each accepted detection extends signalIds and detections, then returns a structured clone of the entire cumulative group. Ten-minute-spaced caller timestamps permit successive accepted detections.
The daemon derives eventId by adding :detected: and the rule name to the already 180-character Event ID.
The internal record route rejects this derived value through MaxLength(180), which the global validation pipe reports as an unprocessable request.
Failed observation processing requests redelivery; the declared consumer caps deliveries at five but has no terminal-outcome callback to the observation cache.
The rejected reduction bypasses pending.delete at line 206. Cached cloned histories remain reachable for the lifetime of the observation runtime after broker retry exhaustion.

evidence.description: The pending Map has no declared size, expiry, cancellation or terminal-delivery eviction policy. Its only deletion is after successful processing.
The shared ID schema imposes only nonemptiness, so envelope preparation does not reject the public 180-character input.
Global DTO validation applies the internal maximum and uses HTTP 422 for validation failures.
The private API client throws for the 422 response, propagating failure out of observation processing before cleanup.
Five broker deliveries and bounded broker retention do not remove objects retained in the separate observation closure.
The default 65536-byte Event cap and 60-per-minute throttle bound individual input and arrival rate, but not lifetime cached outcomes. The proposed inputs are under one KiB each.
One observation runtime is passed to the shared granted-Project consumer, so retained state occupies the daemon used by other Projects.

blockers: No bounded observation of retained pending entries, cloned-history growth or post-max-delivery cleanup was performed because complete memory and cumulative disk sandbox controls are unavailable.
Actual process-level resource impact and recovery have not been measured; the source trace does not establish a crash, outage or a deployed supervisor's behavior.

validation_plan.local: In a parent-approved sandbox, run createObservations with a Project-correct fake API that enforces the real RecordHauntingDto limit, a mocked gateway and no external Work action. Use at most six unique 180-character low-entropy IDs, one dummy Project/service, runtime.oom, and timestamps eleven minutes apart. Simulate no more than the five declared attempts per record. With a trusted inspection hook in a scratch-only copy, count pending entries and retained Detection instances after terminal attempts and after inputs stop; compare three versus six records without load testing. A regression should reject incompatible IDs before watcher mutation or use bounded derived keys, and must evict terminally refused cached outcomes. Also verify one unrelated dummy Project can still process a normal record.
